title: 10. Exercises: Threading & Multiprocessing Masterclass (Part 2)
objectives: Solve the Threading & Multiprocessing Masterclass exercises without looking at the lesson
Test edge cases and explain your approach

sections.title: Performance and Benchmarking Concurrency — Coding Challenges — Performance Benchmarking
sections.body:
```
CHALLENGE 1:
Build "Comprehensive Concurrency Benchmarker":
- Benchmark 6 strategies: sequential, threads, processes, asyncio,
  thread pool, process pool
- For 3 workload types: CPU-heavy, I/O-heavy, mixed
- Measure: throughput, avg/p95/p99 latency, memory usage, CPU usage
- Generate ASCII chart of speedup vs worker count
- Determine: optimal strategy for each workload type

CHALLENGE 2:
Implement "Amdahl's Law Verifier":
- Instrument your code to measure the serial fraction
- Predict theoretical speedup for N workers
- Measure actual speedup empirically
- Compare prediction vs reality
- Identify: which serial bottlenecks limit your program most
- Suggest: which bottlenecks to parallelize for maximum gain

CHALLENGE 3:
Create "Lock Contention Analyzer":
- Wrap all Lock objects in your program with ContentionProfiler
- Run a concurrent workload (100 threads, 1000 operations)
- Identify: top 3 most contended locks
- For each: suggest a fix (finer granularity, read-write lock, CAS, etc.)
- Implement fixes and re-measure contention

CHALLENGE 4:
Build "Memory Bandwidth Benchmark" for multiprocessing:
- Create shared arrays of varying sizes (1MB, 10MB, 100MB, 1GB)
- Measure: throughput (GB/s) as number of processes increases
- Show: how memory bandwidth saturates with more processes
- Compare: shared memory (mmap) vs Pipe vs Queue for same data size

CHALLENGE 5:
Implement "Task Granularity Optimizer":
- Given a dataset of N items and M workers
- Test: chunksize = 1, 10, 100, N/M, N/(M*4)
- Measure: total time for each chunksize
- Find: optimal chunksize for your specific task and machine
- Create formula: f(task_duration, N, M) → optimal_chunksize

CHALLENGE 6:
Create "Concurrency Stress Tester":
- Starts with 1 worker, doubles every 5 seconds (1, 2, 4, 8, 16...)
- Measures throughput at each level
- Detects: knee of the curve (where adding workers stops helping)
- Identifies: bottleneck (CPU, memory, lock contention, I/O)
- Produces: "max effective concurrency" recommendation

CHALLENGE 7:
Build "Production Load Simulator":
- Realistic workload: 80% reads, 15% writes, 5% deletes
- Variable think time between requests (Poisson distributed)
- Arrival rate: increases from 10 to 1000 req/s over 60 seconds
- Measure: throughput, latency percentiles, error rate, queue depth
- Find: system saturation point (where latency starts increasing)
- Produce: capacity planning report
```
